dossie.semAceite: This student has not accepted the terms yet.
dossie.semDados: Missing data to generate the receipt.
porqueValeItens: Brazilian civil procedure law (art. 441) admits electronic documents as evidence, and MP 2.200-2/2001 recognises signatures without an ICP-Brasil certificate when accepted by the parties — which is the case here.
Date and time come from the server clock, not from the signer's device: they cannot be altered by them.
The SHA-256 hash is the text's fingerprint. Changing a single character changes the whole hash — that is what proves the text was not altered afterwards.
The version is recorded and old versions are never deleted: it is always possible to reconstruct exactly what the person read that day.
Anyone can check the hash themselves, without an account, on the verification page — including a public authority.
dossie.porqueValeLimite: Honest limit: this is a simple electronic signature (Law 14.063/2020), not the qualified one with an ICP-Brasil certificate, which carries an automatic legal presumption of authenticity. What sustains this document is the evidence chain above.
dossie.comoEnviar: To send it to an authority or to the student: download the PDF and attach it to your own email. Sending from your address, rather than having the system dispatch it, keeps the record in your "sent" folder and avoids spam filters — in practice, better proof of delivery.
dossie.semAcessoExclusivo: No access to this course's exclusive content.

verificar.intro: Check whether an acceptance receipt is authentic. Paste the hash shown on the document — verification is open, requires no account and reveals no one's personal data.
verificar.formatoInvalido: A SHA-256 hash has 64 characters, from 0-9 and a-f.
verificar.confereNota: There is an acceptance recorded with exactly this hash. That confirms the receipt's text was not altered after signing. Personal data is not shown here, to protect the signer.
verificar.falhouNota: The lookup failed — this may be a connection issue or a temporary outage. It does NOT mean the receipt is invalid: it only means verification could not be completed right now. Please try again shortly.
verificar.naoConfereNota: This may mean the receipt's text was altered after acceptance, that the hash was copied incompletely, or that the document was not issued by this system. Check that you copied all 64 characters.
comoPassos: Open the PDF receipt and find the recorded SHA-256 hash.
Copy the full terms text reproduced in the receipt.
Compute the SHA-256 of that text using any tool you trust.
Compare it with the document's hash: identical means intact; different means altered.

dashboard.title: Welcome to your panel — one step at a time
dashboard.intro: Think of it this way: the course is a bookshelf, modules are the shelves and lessons are the books. You build it top-down, calmly.
steps: Create the course below, in "New course". A name is enough for now — everything can change later.
Click "Edit" on the course to create modules and, inside them, the lessons.
Inside each lesson you add the video, the text, the materials and decide if it is free or paid.
While the switch says "Draft", nobody sees it. Flip it to "Published" only when you are happy.
Use "Preview" anytime to see exactly what a student sees.
dashboard.tip: Nothing here is final. Create, test and delete freely — while it is a draft, it is yours alone.

courseEditor.title: Building the skeleton of the course
courseEditor.intro: This is where you organise the order of things. It is like writing the table of contents before the chapters.
steps: Fill in title and description in Portuguese and English (the site switches languages by itself).
Create modules: the big blocks, like "Module 1 — Fundamentals".
Inside each module, add the lessons in teaching order.
Hold the little dot on the left and drag to reorder modules and lessons.
Click the pencil on a lesson to open its editor and add the video.
courseEditor.tip: Course cover: use a horizontal image (16:9). That is the big one shown in the catalog.

lessonEditor.title: Lesson editor — each tab handles one thing
lessonEditor.intro: This is where the lesson comes alive. No need to fill everything at once; save what you did and come back later.
steps: Video: choose where the video comes from (Vimeo, YouTube or your own upload) and check the preview.
Content: title, summary and lesson text, in both languages.
Materials: PDFs, links and support files for students to download.
Subtitles: generate or paste the captions for the video.
AI Tutor: the summary that teaches the AI to answer questions about this lesson.
Access: sets whether the lesson is free (a taster) or exclusive to paying students.
lessonEditor.tip: Each tab has its own "Save" button. Once saved, it is stored — you can close without worry.

lessonVideo.title: How to put the video in the lesson
lessonVideo.intro: You have two paths, and both look the same to the student.
steps: Fast path (free): upload to YouTube or Vimeo, copy the link or video number and paste it into "ID or link". Pick the right source above.
Direct path: drag the file from your computer into the upload area below. It stays as a draft on our server (up to 500 MB).
Always fill in "Original file" — the folder path on your computer. One day you will need to re-upload and you will thank yourself.
Move the "Production status" along as you go: idea → recorded → edited → subtitled → published.
Check the preview below to make sure the video plays.
lessonVideo.tip: Paid and free videos use the same screen. Access is controlled by the "Access" tab, not by where the video is hosted.

lessonContent.title: The text next to the video
lessonContent.intro: Students read this beside the player. Write like you talk: what they will learn and why it matters.
steps: Title: short and direct, like a headline.
Description: two or three lines summarising the lesson.
Content: the full text, step by step, list of materials, warnings.
Fill in the (EN) fields too — if empty, English students see the Portuguese text.
lessonContent.tip: You do not have to write it all today. Save the draft and come back when the idea is riper.

lessonMaterials.title: Support materials
lessonMaterials.intro: Everything the student downloads or consults: PDF, diagram, parts list, shop link.
steps: Give it a name the student understands, like "Parts list — Lesson 3".
Paste the file link (Drive, manufacturer site, etc.).
Add as many as you like; they show up as a list on the lesson page.
lessonMaterials.tip: Shop and component links age fast. Worth reviewing now and then.

lessonSubtitles.title: Subtitles, made simple
lessonSubtitles.intro: Subtitles help people watching without sound and open the course to English speakers.
steps: Generate automatic captions from the lesson audio.
Read and fix technical terms — machines get proper names wrong.
Save. The captions then appear in the student player.
lessonSubtitles.tip: Always review the Portuguese captions before translating. A translated mistake becomes two mistakes.

lessonTutor.title: Teaching the AI tutor
lessonTutor.intro: The tutor answers student questions about this lesson. It only knows what you tell it here.
steps: Generate the automatic summary from the lesson content.
Add what the AI could never guess: cautions, values, brands, limits of what may be said.
Save. From then on the tutor stays on topic instead of making things up.
lessonTutor.tip: It is also worth writing what the tutor must NOT say (for example, anything sounding like a medical diagnosis).

lessonAccess.title: Free or exclusive? One click decides
lessonAccess.intro: This switch is the gatekeeper of the lesson. It works the same for YouTube videos and for videos hosted by us.
steps: Free lesson: any visitor can watch. Great for opening lessons that work as an invitation.
Exclusive lesson: only enrolled students can open the player.
Change your mind anytime — it takes effect immediately.
lessonAccess.tip: A good recipe: first two lessons of each module open, the rest exclusive.

videoLibrary.title: Your video shelf
videoLibrary.intro: All videos together, even those not yet used in a lesson. This is your inventory.
steps: Use search and filters to find by title, status or source.
"Used in" shows which lesson uses that video — and warns when it is unused.
The original-file field stores the path on your computer; click copy and paste it into your file explorer.
The pending panel lists what still lives only on our server, waiting to move to Vimeo one day.
videoLibrary.tip: The same video can be used in more than one lesson. No need to upload twice.

students.title: Who is studying with you
students.intro: List of enrolled people and how far each one has gone.
steps: See who joined, which course they are in and how much they watched.
Use it to spot where people get stuck — that is usually where an explanation is missing.
Paid enrolments will show up here automatically once payments are switched on.
students.tip: If students always disappear after the same lesson, the problem is probably the lesson, not the students.

security.title: Security and documents
security.subtitle: Where the evidence of your electronic acceptance is kept.
security.howIntro: When you accept the terms, the system stores a set of evidence that allows the exact accepted text to be reconstructed.
howItems: Identification with the tax ID checked on the server.
Full text shown on screen, with no external link.
Mandatory scrolling to the end before acceptance is enabled.
Active acceptance: checkbox you ticked plus your typed full name.
Date and time recorded by the server, not by your computer.
Originating IP address of the request.
SHA-256 hash of the exact text and the term version number.
security.noDocs: You have not registered any acceptance yet.
security.challengeIntro: If the acceptance is ever challenged, this is the path:
challengeItems: Download the PDF receipt: it carries the acceptance data and the full text.
Check that the hash printed on the PDF matches the hash of the term version stored in the system.
The record cannot be edited or deleted by anyone inside the application.
Any text change creates a new version; the signed version stays untouched.

faq.q: Do I have to accept again on every visit?
faq.a: No. Acceptance is registered once per student.
A new version is created. What you signed stays stored exactly as it was.
You and the platform administration. The data protection officer is named in the terms.

faq.q: How long are the records kept?
faq.a: At least five years after the relationship ends, as a legal obligation.

servidor.comFFmpeg: FFmpeg active — automatic duration and thumbnail
servidor.semFFmpeg: no FFmpeg — duration and thumbnail stay manual
servidor.comoLigar: This is normal — the drive may be unplugged. To start it:
servidor.passo1: Plug the external drive into the computer.
servidor.passo3: Come back here and click “Check again”.
servidor.porqueNaoAutomatico: There is no button to start it from here: a website cannot launch programs on your computer — and that very restriction is what protects you on every other site.
servidor.ajudaNada: check that you are at the ROOT of the drive — the file sits next to the midia folder, not inside it.
servidor.ajudaNode: install Node from nodejs.org, or unzip the portable version into servidor/node/ on the drive — then it runs on any computer with nothing installed.
servidor.ajudaOutroPc: nothing to set up again. Plug the drive in and double-click the same file; it finds the disk on its own, whatever letter it gets.

simulacao.seloAjuda: Sample content — not real data from your course.
simulacao.intro: See how each panel screen looks, using sample data. Useful to learn the features and check the layout without needing real content. The screens are the real ones — only the data is made up.
simulacao.ligadaTexto: Showing screens with sample data. Everything that is a sample carries the badge.
simulacao.desligadaTexto: Sample screens are hidden. Turn it on to see them.
simulacao.ligarParaVer: Turn simulation on to see the screens with sample data.
simulacao.t1Texto: A server runs from inside the external drive and reads videos straight from the folders. Works on both computers, nothing to install.
simulacao.t1p1: Plug the drive in and double-click INICIAR-SERVIDOR.bat at the disk root.
simulacao.t1p2: Copy videos into the midia folder, arranged as course / module / lesson.
simulacao.t1p3: Click Scan for new files: duration and thumbnail fill themselves in.
simulacao.t2Texto: Every video and course can have its own cover. Click the image and pick a file — or let the server grab a frame from the video itself.
simulacao.t2p1: On the catalogue or in the Library, click the thumbnail you want to change.
simulacao.t2p2: Choose a 16:9 image up to 5 MB, or paste a link.
simulacao.t2p3: To generate automatically: keep the drive server running and scan the library.
simulacao.t3Texto: The server transcribes the audio and builds the subtitle with word-level timing — the highlight-each-word effect, like CapCut. You choose who transcribes: Groq, OpenAI or your own computer.
simulacao.t3p1: On the server screen, pick the engine and paste the key (Groq has a free daily quota).
simulacao.t3p2: Click Generate subtitle on the video. Long videos are split automatically.
simulacao.t3p3: In the lesson editor, use Pull subtitle to bring the finished file over.
simulacao.t4Texto: With the Portuguese track saved, an English translation is generated preserving every timing.
simulacao.t4p1: Save the Portuguese track in the lesson editor.
simulacao.t4p2: Click Translate and review: technical terms usually need a fix.

simulacao.seguro3: Once published it opens for administrators only; on the development machine it opens directly.
